title: fix(plugin-pinyin-search): the boot companion pass no longer holds readiness, and an unchanged restart reads no rows
body:
Fixes #25634

Clause-②: yes
Metadata-protocol: none

## What was wrong (measured on `main` 9dac9eb8d6)

- `PinyinSearchPlugin.start()` hooks `kernel:bootstrapped` and awaits `backfillSearchCompanion(engine, …)`.
- `ObjectKernel.bootstrap()` awaits `kernel:ready`, then `kernel:bootstrapped`, then `kernel:listening` (`packages/core/src/kernel.ts`, the boot-phase block). `kernel:listening` is where the HTTP server opens its socket. So the backfill held readiness for as long as the walk took.
- The walk reads every row of every `__search`-bearing object (`keysetWalk`, 1,000 rows per page) and decides per row in JavaScript. A clean second boot repeats the same full read, because `__search = null` means both "never inspected" and "inspected, no CJK".

## What this changes

All changes are inside `packages/plugins/plugin-pinyin-search`, plus the census regeneration listed below.

1. **Off the readiness path.** `kernel:bootstrapped` now *starts* the boot pass and returns without awaiting it. Writes made meanwhile are stamped by the companion hooks, which are bound at `kernel:ready` as before. A failure is logged at `warn`, not swallowed. `destroy()` aborts the pass between pages and awaits it, so it ends before the datasource plugin (destroyed after it) closes the pool. The kernel's hook dispatch is unchanged: no other plugin's contract moves.
2. **An unchanged second boot reads nothing.** When a walk of an object completes, the pass writes a completion record into **one `sys_migration` row** (`id: 'pinyin-search-companion'`). It stores, per object, the source fields and `since` (the walk's start, minus a 10-minute clock margin). A later boot walks only `updated_at >= since AND __search IS NULL`. This is the rows written since the last walk that still have no companion: rows written while the switch was off, seed rows written before the hooks were bound, and hook-bypassing writes that kept the audit stamp. Neither half of that filter works alone. `__search IS NULL` alone matches every non-CJK row forever, which is the card's point. `updated_at` alone matches every row the walk itself filled, because the walk's writes go through the non-bypassable audit stamp; that was measured red on the first draft of this branch. A changed source field, a different `SEARCH_COMPANION_RECONCILE_VERSION`, or a scan with a failed page or skipped row leaves that object to be walked in full again.
3. **Explicit rebuild unchanged.** `rebuildSearchCompanion()` (the `force: true` alias) still walks every row. It is the path for writers that bypass the hooks *and* back-date `updated_at`.
4. **Stale-blob guard.** The walk now runs while the server takes writes. Before writing a row, it re-reads that row by id (only rows about to be written pay this), so a rename that landed after the page was read is not overwritten with the old name's blob.

### The store: `sys_migration`, and why it is not a protocol surface

- It is the existing deployment ledger for "has THIS deployment run this data pass" (`platform-objects/src/system/sys-migration.object.ts`). Its API is read-only (`apiMethods: ['get', 'list']`).
- The receipt is written through the engine against the spec row contract `DataMigrationFlagSchema`. That is the same shape as the seed-tenancy receipt (`metadata-protocol/src/migrations/seed-tenancy-backfill.ts`, the ruled A″-2 route), whose id is spelled in its own package.
- The id here is a constant of this package, not of `@objectstack/spec`: there is one writer and one reader, both here. Field reading: `verified_at: null` (no self-check), `blocking: 0` (no consumer is gated on it), `advisory` = rows skipped in the last run.
- No new spec key, setting, env var or metadata marker. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.
- A kernel without `sys_migration` (no `PlatformObjectsPlugin`) keeps the old cost, a full walk each boot (now after readiness), and says so once at `warn`.
- `sys_inbox_message` keeps `searchable` as it is. Search is untouched, so nothing a user reads is narrowed.

### Published surface (additive only)

- `CompanionBackfillResult.pages`
- `CompanionBackfillOptions.signal`
- `PinyinSearchPlugin.whenReconciled()`
- `@objectstack/spec` added as a runtime dependency (already in the closure through `@objectstack/objectql`).
- One `patch` changeset. These three additions widen the package's public surface, so the PR declares `Clause-②: yes` (the API is additive, there is no metadata-protocol change, and `patch` stays).

## Proof

All tests run through the real `ObjectKernel`, the real ObjectQL engine and `SqlDriver` on a **SQLite file** (two boots share one database), with the real `SysMigration` object (`src/boot-reconcile.integration.test.ts`):

| pin | reading |
|---|---|
| first boot vs unchanged second boot (the card's regression test) | first boot **2500 rows / 3 queries**; unchanged second boot **0 rows / 1 query** (one filtered query answering no row) |
| hook-bypassing row added after the last walk | second boot reads **1** row and fills it (`lina ln`) |
| control: normal ObjectQL write while the pass is parked on page 1 | `__search` = `wangfang wf` at once |
| control: explicit rebuild (`force`) | walks **2501 / 2501** rows and fills a back-dated row no watermark sees |
| readiness | `bootstrap()` (through `kernel:listening`) resolves while the pass's first page is held; the pass then completes |
| shutdown mid-walk | stops after page 2 of 3, writes no receipt; the next boot walks all 2500 |
| no ledger | every boot walks every row (the old cost, never a missed row) |
| failure logged | a throwing pass logs `warn` `companion reconcile failed` with the error |

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-pinyin-search test` ⇒ Test Files 4 passed, Tests 39 passed. `typecheck` (tsc and `check:test-typecheck`) clean. `eslint --no-inline-config packages/plugins/plugin-pinyin-search` exit 0.

**Ablations** (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty; tests import `./*.js` relatively, so the run reads `src/` and no `dist` build is involved):

- Drop the completion record (`previous = undefined`) ⇒ 2 red: `expected { queries: 3, rows: 2500 } to deeply equal { queries: 1, rows: 0 }`, and `expected 2501 to be 1`. Restored blob `08208bf4cabb`.
- Await the pass inside `kernel:bootstrapped` again ⇒ the readiness pin goes red (`bootstrap()` never resolves while the page is held: test timed out). The first attempt at this leg was refused by the tool as a no-op (the replacement contained its anchor) and did not run; it was re-run with a disjoint replacement. Restored blob `28739311a522`.

## Scale note: 100 k rows, boot-to-ready, same harness both times

100,000 rows inserted straight through the driver (no hooks, `updated_at` back-dated, every 10th row CJK). SQLite file, one run each on a shared box. "Ready" = `kernel.bootstrap()` resolved, which includes `kernel:listening`.

| | `main` 9dac9eb8d6 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| first boot of an existing deployment, ready | **11,946 ms** | **293 ms** (the 100 k-row walk then finishes 14,352 ms after start, after readiness) |
| unchanged second boot, ready | **1,033 ms** (re-reads all 100 k rows) | **676 ms** (pass done at 696 ms, 0 rows read) |

The branch's first-boot walk is about 20% slower than `main`'s, from the re-read before each of the 10 k writes. It is paid once, after readiness. `main`'s second boot grows linearly with rows (production: 6.7 M rows, about 4 min 50 s on PostgreSQL). The branch's second boot reads no row. The filtered query is a scan the database runs, not rows moved into JavaScript.

## Gates (local)

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **111** commands at head `fbbc0bc41`. All 111 were run, each exit code captured before any pipe, and every one **exited 0**. `--ran` verdict: `111 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 111 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`. Two of them, `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, first exited 3 (no built `dist/` in a fresh worktree); they exited 0 after `pnpm build`.
- Red on the way, fixed in this PR:
  - `check:tenant-audit-census`: the receipt upsert is one new engine write call site (system context, object name an imported constant). After merging `main` (which had itself moved to 239), the census is 240. Regenerated with `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`. The eight hand-written prose figures the gate names were updated in `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` (239 → 240, 76 → 77, 136 → 137). The historical "135 (77%)" claim the page quotes was left as quoted.
  - `check:engine-double-contract`: the failure-path test's fake engine carried an unused `update`; dropped.
  - `check:test-source-alias`: `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects/system` and `@objectstack/spec/system` are aliased to source in this package's `vitest.config.ts`. The registry entry is unchanged.
  - `check:query-options-erasure`: the new test's three `as any` casts on query options were removed.
  - `check:optional-error-sink` (red in CI's `Lint · docs & code guards` at `8b1dea30b`): this PR had added an optional `error` channel to `MinimalLogger` beside an optional `warn`, a sink type that allows silence. Nothing calls `logger.error`, so the member was removed (`fbbc0bc41`), restoring `main`'s shape. Local exit 0. `dispatch-gates --commands` does not name this gate for this diff, so the derived list misses it.
- Merge of `origin/main` at head `8b1dea30b` (merge commit, no rebase). `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`, `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` conflicted. All three were taken from `main` and regenerated: `pnpm install` for the lockfile, `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write` for the census pair. On the merged head:
  - `node scripts/check-tenant-audit-census.mjs` exit 0 (`240 write call sites certified`), and its `--self-test` exit 0.
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` exit 0 (`This diff introduces no major bump`; the LEVEL axis reads NOT APPLICABLE locally because no `pull_request` payload exists).
  - `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` exit 0 (`this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset`).
  - Both scripts' `--self-test` exit 0.
  - After rebuilding the closure, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-pinyin-search test` passed (4 files, 39 tests) and `typecheck` exit 0. Re-run at `fbbc0bc41` with the same result; scoped eslint exit 0.
- `eslint --no-inline-config packages/plugins/plugin-pinyin-search` (the `pnpm lint` command, scoped to this package): exit 0.
- Every family CI runs (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core) is read from this PR's check-runs, not re-run here.
- `Spec property liveness` is red on `main` since 0189524a4 (#25734), not from this PR: `translation/flows.screens` cites `engine.ts`, whose only `screens` mention moved to `run-resume.ts`; it reproduces on `origin/main` without this PR.

## Acceptance notes

- Pre-existing, not changed here: the pass's companion write goes through `engine.update`, so the audit stamp moves a filled record's `updated_at` / `updated_by` to the system at the moment of the fill. That was already true of the old boot backfill and of `rebuildSearchCompanion`. The stamp is non-bypassable by design (`audit-stamp-skip-automations.test.ts`).
- First boot after upgrading: each companion-bearing object is walked in full once more (no receipt yet), now after readiness. On the production deployment that is the 6.7 M-row walk, once, off the boot path. It rewrites only CJK rows that lack a blob, as before; non-CJK rows are never written.
- `#23122` is not addressed here (it explains the inbox volume, not the scan).
